royal-flush: Ten through ace, all one suit: the best hand there is
straight-flush: Five in a row, all in one suit
four-of-a-kind: Every card of one rank, plus a kicker
flush: Five cards of one suit, in any order
straight: Five ranks in a row, mixed suits
three-of-a-kind: Trips: three cards of one rank
two-pair: Two different matched sets of two
one-pair: Just two cards of matching rank
high-card: Nothing matches, so the top card plays
spades: The black suit shaped like an upturned leaf; trumps in a game named after it
hearts: The red suit of love, and a trick-avoiding game
diamonds: The red suit shaped like a rhombus
clubs: The black suit shaped like a clover
ace: Can play high or low; one pip in the middle
two: The lowest numbered card, sometimes called a deuce
eight: Crazy, in a classic shedding game
nine: One below the highest number card
jack: The lowest face card, often shown in profile
queen: The only face card that's usually a woman
king: The highest face card; one of them seems to stab himself
uno-skip: The next player loses their turn
uno-draw-two: The next player picks up a pair and loses their turn
uno-wild-draw-four: Call a color and make the next player pick up four
